title: Civil Summons / Writ — State of Missouri, Cedar County — Thomas Smith v. James M. Wrenn, 1867
text:
WRITS — CIVIL SUITS — SENTINEL PRINT, BOLIVAR, MO.

STATE OF MISSOURI, }
County of Cedar     } ss.  any disinterested white person over the age of 21 years
The State of Missouri, to the Sheriff of    of Fannin County, Texas: Greeting:

YOU ARE HEREBY COMMANDED to summons

James M. Wrenn

if he be found in your county, to be and appear before the Cedar Circuit Court,
on the first day of the next term thereof, to be begun and held at the court house in said county,
on the 3d Monday in March next, then and there to answer the
petition of Thomas Smith

and have you then and there this writ, and do you certify to our said court how you execute this
writ.

In Testimony Whereof, I, Q. H. Cannaway, Clerk
of said Court, have hereunto set my hand and seal of
said Court. Done at Stockton this
14th day of January, A.D., 1867.
Q. H. Cannaway
CLERK.
notes: Printed writ form (Sentinel Print, Bolivar, MO) with handwritten entries. Summons directed to the Sheriff of Fannin County, Texas to serve James M. Wrenn to appear before the Cedar Circuit Court, Missouri on the 3rd Monday in March. Case: Thomas Smith (plaintiff) vs. James M. Wrenn. Clerk: Q. H. Cannaway, Stockton, MO. Interesting that the summons was directed to Fannin County, Texas sheriff, suggesting Wrenn had relocated to Texas by 1867.
